##### destroy(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override public void destroy()`
- **Summary:** Removes this bean's context from the holder when Spring destroys it, including after a failed context refresh.
- **Contract:**
  - Removes this bean's context from the holder when Spring destroys it, including after a failed context refresh.
  - <p> Two boundaries are accepted: if this bean's own creation fails after the setter has run (for example a {@code BeanPostProcessor} throws), Spring never registers it as disposable, so the holder keeps that context registered until the holder is cleared (a context registered later takes precedence while it remains registered); and destroying this bean individually while its context is still running removes that running context from the holder, because Spring does not tell a destruction callback why it is invoked.
- **Parameters:**

##### onApplicationEvent(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override public void onApplicationEvent(final ContextClosedEvent event)`
- **Summary:** Removes the closed context from the holder; any other registered context (for example the parent of a closed child context) remains available.
- **Parameters:**
  - `event` (`ContextClosedEvent`) — the context shutdown event.
##### getBean(...) -> Object
- **Signature:** `public Object getBean(final String name) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, NoSuchBeanDefinitionException, BeansException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves a bean from the Spring ApplicationContext by its name.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns {@code null} only when no context is registered: none has been injected yet, or every registered context has since closed or had its bridge bean destroyed.
  - If a context is registered but no bean with the given name exists, {@code NoSuchBeanDefinitionException} is thrown.
- **Parameters:**
  - `name` (`String`) — the name of the bean to retrieve.
- **Returns:** the bean instance, or {@code null} if no ApplicationContext is registered (none injected yet, or all released after close/destruction).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the supplied context has not been refreshed or has already been closed.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the context is initialized and {@code name} is {@code null} .
  - `org.springframework.beans.factory.NoSuchBeanDefinitionException` — if no bean with the specified name is found.
  - `org.springframework.beans.BeansException` — if the initialized context cannot create or retrieve the bean.

  - `org.springframework.beans.BeansException` — if the initialized context cannot create or retrieve the bean.

### Class SpringTransactionTracker (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker)
Tells this library, from a Spring transaction manager, when each transaction it runs is committed or rolled back, so that the library follows the transaction that actually owns a data source's connection.

**Modifiers:** `public final`
**Implements:** `TransactionExecutionListener`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public SpringTransactionTracker()` — Creates a tracker.

#### Public Static Methods
##### unresolvedTransactions(...) -> List<UnresolvedTransaction>
- **Signature:** `public static List<UnresolvedTransaction> unresolvedTransactions()`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable snapshot of transactions with cache-affecting writes and failed or missing completion reports.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** unresolved transactions, ordered by ID
##### unresolvedTransactionCount(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int unresolvedTransactionCount()`
- **Summary:** Returns the current monitoring count; concurrent completion or failure can change it immediately.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** number of unresolved transactions with cache-affecting writes
##### confirmSettled(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean confirmSettled(final long transactionId)`
- **Summary:** Acknowledges externally verified settlement of one unresolved transaction and allows its cache blocks to expire on the next read.
- **Contract:**
  - The caller must establish that all its pending work has committed, rolled back or otherwise cannot commit later, including work left by failed cleanup.
  - Nothing releases a block automatically, neither elapsed time nor garbage collection: nothing bounds when pending work may still commit.
- **Parameters:**
  - `transactionId` (`long`) — ID from {@link #unresolvedTransactions()} or its warning log
- **Returns:** {@code true} if this call resolved the record; {@code false} if it was already resolved or is unknown
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the ID belongs to a transaction still active with no failure report
- **Signature:** `public static List<Long> confirmSettled(final Collection<Long> transactionIds) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Acknowledges the externally verified settlement of each of the given unresolved transactions, and of no other (see {@link #confirmSettled(long)} for what the caller must establish first).
- **Contract:**
  - Acknowledges the externally verified settlement of each of the given unresolved transactions, and of no other (see {@link #confirmSettled(long)} for what the caller must establish first).
  - Nothing is confirmed if one of them belongs to a transaction still active with no failure report.
- **Parameters:**
  - `transactionIds` (`Collection<Long>`) — the IDs, from {@link #unresolvedTransactions()} or the warning log
- **Returns:** the IDs this call resolved, in the order given, without duplicates
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code transactionIds} or one of its elements is {@code null}
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if one of the IDs belongs to a transaction still active with no failure report
##### register(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void register(final ConfigurableTransactionManager... transactionManagers) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a tracker with each of {@code transactionManagers} , before their other execution listeners (see the registration requirements above), replacing any tracker registered with them before.
- **Parameters:**
  - `transactionManagers` (`ConfigurableTransactionManager[]`) — the transaction managers, such as {@code DataSourceTransactionManager} , {@code JdbcTransactionManager} or {@code JpaTransactionManager}
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code transactionManagers} or one of them is {@code null}

##### connection(...) -> Connection
- **Signature:** `public Connection connection() throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Returns the JDBC connection of the transaction.
- **Contract:**
  - It is shared by all scopes of the transaction and must not be closed manually: the outermost scope releases it when the transaction completes.
  - The returned reference must only be used while the transaction is open; this accessor checks the owning thread, but does not check whether the transaction has completed and released the connection.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** the JDBC connection used by the transaction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if called from a thread other than the transaction's owner thread

- **Parameters:**

##### status(...) -> Status
- **Signature:** `public Status status()`
- **Summary:** Returns the current status of the transaction this scope belongs to: {@link Status#ACTIVE} until the transaction is marked rollback-only ( {@link Status#MARKED_ROLLBACK} ) or the outermost scope completes.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code try (SqlTransaction tran = JdbcUtil.beginTransaction(dataSource)) { if (tran.status() == SqlTransaction.Status.ACTIVE) { // The transaction can still be committed } } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the current transaction status, never {@code null}
- **See also:** Status
##### isActive(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isActive()`
- **Summary:** Checks whether the transaction this scope belongs to is active, i.e.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code try (SqlTransaction tran = JdbcUtil.beginTransaction(dataSource)) { if (tran.isActive()) { performDatabaseOperations(); } } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} if the transaction is active, {@code false} otherwise
##### commit(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void commit() throws IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException`
- **Summary:** Commits this scope.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> A nested scope's commit only completes the scope: the database {@code COMMIT} is issued when the outermost scope commits.
  - If the transaction has been marked rollback-only (a nested scope rolled back, typically because its failure was caught and the work went on), the outermost commit rolls back instead and throws {@link RollbackOnlyException} : none of the transaction's work was committed.
  - If the rollback fails, its failure is thrown instead (such as the {@link UncheckedSQLException} of the rollback), as is an unchecked failure of the connection cleanup after the rollback; the reason the commit failed is attached to it as a suppressed exception (a {@code RollbackOnlyException} once the transaction has been rolled back, an {@code IllegalStateException} otherwise).
  - </p> <p> Scopes opened inside this one that are still open when it commits were never completed (for example, a nested scope whose code threw before its {@code commit()} and has no {@code finally} block): they are exited, the transaction is marked rollback-only, and this method throws: an outermost scope rolls the transaction back and throws {@link RollbackOnlyException} (or the failure of the rollback, as above), a nested scope throws {@link IllegalStateException} .
  - If restoring an isolation level while exiting such a scope fails with an unchecked exception, that exception is thrown instead (by an outermost scope, after the same rollback).
  - </p> <p> If the driver fails to restore the enclosing scope's isolation level when this nested scope exits, the failure propagates (an SQL error as an {@link UncheckedSQLException} , a runtime exception or an error as it is) and this scope stays open, so its {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} can complete it.
  - </p> <p> When the outermost scope actually commits, the status becomes {@link Status#COMMITTED} on success.
  - On failure the transaction is rolled back automatically, leaving the status {@link Status#ROLLED_BACK} (or {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK} if that rollback also fails).
  - For a transaction participating in a Spring-managed transaction, the outermost commit issues no database {@code COMMIT} : it completes the transaction and releases the connection to Spring, which commits the work when its transaction completes; a rollback-only one marks the Spring transaction rollback-only and throws {@link RollbackOnlyException} , or the failure of the mark (the status is then {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK} ; see {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} ).
  - If the Spring transaction has completed already (the scope was left open past it), or runs its {@code afterCommit} or {@code afterCompletion} callbacks (the scope was left open into them), the commit throws {@link IllegalStateException} and the status becomes {@link Status#FAILED_COMMIT} : Spring decided the outcome of the work without it (see row 27 of the completion scenarios for what is detected).
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if called from a thread other than the transaction's owner thread, if a scope opened inside this one was never completed, if this scope has already completed (committed, rolled back, its commit failed, or an enclosing scope completed and exited it while it was still open), if the outermost commit of a participating transaction marked rollback-only cannot mark the Spring transaction rollback-only (see {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} ), or if the Spring-managed transaction a participating transaction participates in has completed, or begun to complete, before its outermost commit
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if an SQL error occurs while restoring the enclosing scope's isolation level (the scope then stays open, so its {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} can complete it), committing, or rolling back a rollback-only transaction. A failed database commit triggers an automatic rollback; any rollback failure is suppressed on the commit exception.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.RollbackOnlyException` — if this is the outermost scope and the transaction was marked rollback-only, or a scope opened inside this one was never completed: the transaction has been rolled back (a participating transaction: the Spring-managed transaction has been marked rollback-only, so Spring rolls back the work)
##### rollback(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public void rollback() throws IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException`
- **Summary:** Rolls back this scope.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> A nested scope's rollback marks the transaction rollback-only ( {@link Status#MARKED_ROLLBACK} ); the database {@code ROLLBACK} is issued when the outermost scope completes, whether it commits or rolls back.
  - The outermost rollback sets the status to {@link Status#ROLLED_BACK} (or {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK} if the rollback fails), restores the connection's original state and releases it (after a failed rollback, aborts and releases it without restoring its state).
  - The scope is always exited, as by {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} : if the enclosing scope's isolation level cannot be restored, the transaction stays marked rollback-only; an {@link SQLException} from the connection is logged, while a {@link RuntimeException} or an {@link Error} is thrown after the scope has been exited (it used to leave a nested scope open, and the transaction {@link Status#ACTIVE} , after an explicit rollback).
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if called from a thread other than the transaction's owner thread, if this scope has already completed, or if the outermost rollback of a participating transaction cannot mark the Spring transaction rollback-only (see {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} ; the status is then {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if an SQL error occurs during the outermost rollback
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if marking the Spring transaction rollback-only fails with another exception (an {@link Error} from the mark propagates as well); the status is then {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK}
##### rollbackIfNotCommitted(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void rollbackIfNotCommitted() throws IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException`
- **Summary:** Ends this scope, rolling it back unless it has completed: a no-op after {@link #commit()} or {@link #rollback()} of this scope, and on any further call.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> A nested scope that is ended this way marks the transaction {@link Status#MARKED_ROLLBACK} ; the database {@code ROLLBACK} is issued when the outermost scope completes.
  - The scope is always exited: if the enclosing scope's isolation level cannot be restored on the connection, the transaction stays marked rollback-only; an {@link SQLException} from the connection is logged, while a {@link RuntimeException} or an {@link Error} is propagated after the scope has been exited.
  - If the Spring transaction cannot be marked (no connection holder is bound to the data source any more, a JPA transaction that owns the connection refuses the mark or can no longer be identified, the completion of the Spring transaction has started so that the mark can't change its outcome any more, see {@link #commit()} , or the mark throws), the rollback fails with an {@link IllegalStateException} (or the mark's own failure), the status becomes {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK} (Spring may still commit the work), and the in-memory changes tied to the work (such as generated IDs written back to entities) are not undone but left to the Spring transaction's outcome.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if called from a thread other than the transaction's owner thread, or if the outermost rollback of a participating transaction cannot mark the Spring transaction rollback-only (see above); the status is then {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK}
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if an SQL error occurs during the outermost rollback
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if marking the Spring transaction rollback-only fails with another exception (an {@link Error} from the mark propagates as well); the status is then {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK}
##### runOutsideTransaction(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Throwable> void runOutsideTransaction(final Throwables.Runnable<E> cmd) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Executes {@code cmd} outside of this transaction: the transaction is unregistered from the current thread while {@code cmd} runs, so operations on the data source inside it acquire their own connections and commit independently, and it is registered again afterwards (if it is still active or marked rollback-only).
- **Contract:**
  - Executes {@code cmd} outside of this transaction: the transaction is unregistered from the current thread while {@code cmd} runs, so operations on the data source inside it acquire their own connections and commit independently, and it is registered again afterwards (if it is still active or marked rollback-only).
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code try (SqlTransaction tran = JdbcUtil.beginTransaction(dataSource)) { dao.update(entity); tran.runOutsideTransaction(() -> auditDao.insert(auditRecord)); // committed even if tran rolls back tran.commit(); } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`Throwables.Runnable<E>`) — the {@code Runnable} to be executed outside of this transaction, must not be {@code null}
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if called from a thread other than the transaction's owner thread, or if, after {@code cmd} completes normally, another transaction has been opened on this thread for the same data source and was not closed: it is rolled back, as by {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} of its outermost scope, and this transaction registered again (if {@code cmd} throws, that condition is attached to its exception as a suppressed exception)
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code cmd} is {@code null}
  - `E` — if the {@code Runnable} throws an exception
##### callOutsideTransaction(...) -> R
- **Signature:** `public <R, E extends Throwable> R callOutsideTransaction(final Throwables.Callable<? extends R, E> cmd) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Executes {@code cmd} outside of this transaction and returns its result; see {@link #runOutsideTransaction(Throwables.Runnable)} .
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`Throwables.Callable<? extends R, E>`) — the {@code Callable} to be executed outside of this transaction, must not be {@code null}
- **Returns:** the result returned by the {@code Callable}
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — see {@link #runOutsideTransaction(Throwables.Runnable)}
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code cmd} is {@code null}
  - `E` — if the {@code Callable} throws an exception
##### close(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override public void close() throws IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException`
- **Summary:** Ends this scope by calling {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} , so the scope can be used in a try-with-resources block: a no-op after {@link #commit()} , and on any further call.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code try (SqlTransaction tran = JdbcUtil.beginTransaction(dataSource)) { dao.save(entity); tran.commit(); } // close() rolls back if commit() was not reached } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if called from a thread other than the transaction's owner thread, or if the outermost rollback of a participating transaction cannot mark the Spring transaction rollback-only (see {@link #rollbackIfNotCommitted()} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if an SQL error occurs during the outermost rollback
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if marking the Spring transaction rollback-only fails with another exception (an {@link Error} from the mark propagates as well); the status is then {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK}
- **See also:** #rollbackIfNotCommitted()
##### toString(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `@Override public String toString()`
- **Summary:** Returns a string representation of this scope, including the transaction's identifier.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a string representation of this scope

### Enum Status (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SqlTransaction.Status)
The status of a transaction, shared by all its scopes (see {@link SqlTransaction#status()} ).

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Enum Constants
- `ACTIVE` — The transaction is open and not marked rollback-only: the status from its beginning until it is marked rollback-only or its outermost scope completes.
- `MARKED_ROLLBACK` — The transaction can only end rolled back: a nested scope rolled back (for example, its work threw and its cleanup call ended it), a scope completed while a scope opened inside it was still open, or the exit of a nested scope could not restore the enclosing scope's isolation level.
- `COMMITTED` — The outermost scope committed the transaction: the database {@code COMMIT} succeeded.
- `FAILED_COMMIT` — The outermost commit did not complete.
- `ROLLED_BACK` — The outermost scope rolled the transaction back: its {@link SqlTransaction#rollbackIfNotCommitted()} (or {@link SqlTransaction#close()} , or the deprecated {@link SqlTransaction#rollback()} ) ran without a commit, its commit found the transaction marked rollback-only (or a scope opened inside it still open), or its database commit failed and was rolled back automatically.
- `FAILED_ROLLBACK` — The rollback failed: the database {@code ROLLBACK} threw, and the connection was aborted and released without restoring its auto-commit mode and isolation level.

- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
- (none)

## com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation
### Annotation Bind (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.Bind)
Binds a method parameter to a named parameter in SQL queries.

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### value(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `String value() default ""`
- **Summary:** Specifies the named-parameter token (the part after {@code :} ) that this method parameter should be bound to in the SQL.
- **Contract:**
  - Specifies the named-parameter token (the part after {@code :} ) that this method parameter should be bound to in the SQL.
  - <p> An explicit value is normally required: when a named-query method has more than one statement parameter, every such parameter must carry an {@code @Bind} with a non-empty {@code value} that matches a named parameter in the SQL verbatim.
  - An empty name matches no named parameter, so a named query whose {@code @Bind} names are verified against the static SQL reports {@code IllegalArgumentException} ; the binding setup that rejects an empty {@code @Bind} name outright reports {@code UnsupportedOperationException} , and is the only check left for a positional stored-procedure call or when {@link Query#fragmentsContainNamedParameters()} defers the static-SQL check.
  - (This differs from {@code @SqlFragment} / {@code @BindList} , where an empty value falls back to the method parameter name &mdash; which requires compiling with the {@code -parameters} flag.) </p> <p> <b> Non-empty value: </b> on a named query a name that does not appear in the static SQL fails DAO initialization with {@code IllegalArgumentException} , while two parameters bound to the same name, or a named parameter of the SQL left unbound (the reserved system-time parameters excepted when {@link Query#injectCurrentTimeParameters()} is enabled), fail with {@code UnsupportedOperationException} .
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the named-parameter token to bind to (without the leading colon); empty by default

### Annotation Cache (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.Cache)
Configures the shared DAO cache used by methods with {@link CacheResult} enabled.

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### capacity(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `int capacity() default JdbcUtil.DEFAULT_CACHE_CAPACITY`
- **Summary:** Specifies the maximum number of entries the cache can hold.
- **Contract:**
  - When the cache is at capacity, the underlying pool's eviction policy determines which entries are removed to make room for new ones (the default {@link Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache} relies on the {@code KeyedObjectPool} 's default policy combined with TTL/idle-time-based eviction; see {@link CacheResult#maxLiveTimeMillis()} and {@link CacheResult#maxIdleTimeMillis()} ).
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the maximum number of cache entries
##### evictDelayMillis(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `long evictDelayMillis() default JdbcUtil.DEFAULT_CACHE_EVICT_DELAY`
- **Summary:** Specifies the interval (in milliseconds) at which the background eviction scheduler runs to remove expired entries from the cache.
- **Contract:**
  - This is <em> not </em> the per-entry time-to-live; entry expiration is controlled by {@link CacheResult#maxLiveTimeMillis()} and {@link CacheResult#maxIdleTimeMillis()} when the {@link CacheResult} annotation is used on individual methods.
  - With the default {@link Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache} , {@code 0} disables the background sweep entirely: an expired entry is still never returned (it is discarded when it is next looked up), but it can keep occupying capacity until it is looked up or evicted to make room.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the interval in milliseconds between eviction sweeps
##### impl(...) -> Class<? extends DaoCache>
- **Signature:** `Class<? extends DaoCache> impl() default Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache.class`
- **Summary:** Specifies the implementation class for the DAO cache.
- **Contract:**
  - The implementation must implement {@link DaoCache} and declare a constructor that accepts two parameters: {@code (int capacity, long evictDelay)} .
  - The DAO proxy resolves that exact constructor signature when it creates the cache; a class that does not declare it fails DAO initialization with {@code IllegalArgumentException} (unlike the {@link #capacity()} / {@link #evictDelayMillis()} range violations, which fail with {@code UnsupportedOperationException} ).
  - If the implementation also implements {@link AutoCloseable} , an instance created for a DAO proxy is closed when that proxy is discarded because another thread registered an equivalent proxy first, or once the proxy, evicted from the bounded DAO proxy pool, has become unreachable.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the cache implementation class; defaults to {@link Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache}

### Annotation CacheResult (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.CacheResult)
Enables method-level result caching for DAO query methods.

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### enabled(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean enabled() default false`
- **Summary:** Enables caching when set to {@code true} .
- **Contract:**
  - Enables caching when set to {@code true} .
  - <p> The default is {@code false} ; set this element explicitly when the annotation should activate cache result handling.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} to enable caching, {@code false} (default) to leave it disabled
##### maxLiveTimeMillis(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `long maxLiveTimeMillis() default JdbcUtil.DEFAULT_CACHE_LIVE_TIME`
- **Summary:** Specifies the maximum time (in milliseconds) a cached entry can live.
- **Contract:**
  - Use a positive value: the built-in {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache} rejects {@code 0} when storing a result (see the type-level documentation).
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the maximum cache entry lifetime in milliseconds; defaults to {@link JdbcUtil#DEFAULT_CACHE_LIVE_TIME} (30 minutes)
##### maxIdleTimeMillis(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `long maxIdleTimeMillis() default JdbcUtil.DEFAULT_CACHE_MAX_IDLE_TIME`
- **Summary:** Specifies the maximum idle time (in milliseconds) for a cached entry.
- **Contract:**
  - If an entry is not accessed within this time, it expires and is removed.
  - This is useful for frequently accessed data that should expire if unused.
  - <p> The entry expires when either {@code maxLiveTimeMillis} or {@code maxIdleTimeMillis} is exceeded, whichever comes first.
  - Use a positive value: the built-in {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache} rejects {@code 0} when storing a result (see the type-level documentation).
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code // Expire if not accessed for 10 minutes @CacheResult(enabled = true, maxLiveTimeMillis = 3600000, maxIdleTimeMillis = 600000) @Query("SELECT * FROM user_sessions WHERE token = :token") UserSession getSession(@Bind("token") String token) throws SQLException; } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the maximum idle time in milliseconds; defaults to {@link JdbcUtil#DEFAULT_CACHE_MAX_IDLE_TIME} (3 minutes)
##### minSize(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `int minSize() default 0`
- **Summary:** Specifies the minimum size requirement for caching results.
- **Contract:**
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code // Only cache if result has at least 10 items @CacheResult(enabled = true, minSize = 10) @Query("SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = :category") List<Product> findByCategory(@Bind("category") String category) throws SQLException; } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the minimum result size to cache; the default {@code 0} means no minimum
##### maxSize(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `int maxSize() default Integer.MAX_VALUE`
- **Summary:** Specifies the maximum size limit for caching results.
- **Contract:**
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code // Don't cache if result has more than 1000 items @CacheResult(enabled = true, maxSize = 1000) @Query("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE date >= :startDate") List<Order> findOrdersSince(@Bind("startDate") Date date) throws SQLException; } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the maximum result size to cache; the default {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} means no maximum
##### serialization(...) -> CacheSerialization
- **Signature:** `CacheSerialization serialization() default CacheSerialization.NONE`
- **Summary:** Specifies the serialization strategy for cache storage and retrieval.
- **Contract:**
  - This determines how objects are copied when stored in or retrieved from cache.
  - <p> Available options: </p> <ul> <li> {@link CacheSerialization#NONE} (default) - No serialization, stores direct references </li> <li> {@link CacheSerialization#KRYO} - Uses Kryo to deep-copy result graphs </li> <li> {@link CacheSerialization#JSON} - Uses JSON round trips to create copies </li> </ul> <p> With {@link CacheSerialization#KRYO} or {@link CacheSerialization#JSON} , collections, maps and populated optional/nullable wrappers are copied even when they implement {@link com.landawn.abacus.util.Immutable} .
  - Other top-level {@code Immutable} values are stored and returned as-is; their contents must be deeply immutable to avoid sharing mutable state.
  - Values without this marker pass through the selected serializer even if their Java types are immutable, except that {@link CacheSerialization#JSON} shares {@code java.time} values and enum constants as-is.
  - Unannotated methods used with the thread-local DAO cache select Kryo when its parser is available and JSON otherwise.
  - A top-level collection or map whose non-public class the parser cannot construct (for example that of {@code List.of(...)} ) is rebuilt as the default container of its kind when the method's return type accepts it, and an {@code EnumSet} is copied as an {@code EnumSet} .
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the serialization strategy
- **See also:** <a href="https://github.com/EsotericSoftware/kryo">,Kryo Serialization,</a>
##### cacheNestedResults(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean cacheNestedResults() default true`
- **Summary:** Whether calls made by this cached method may also use inherited type-level result caching.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} to preserve nested type-level result caching; {@code false} to suppress it
##### filter(...) -> String\[\]
- **Signature:** `String[] filter() default { "query", "queryFor", "list", "get", "batchGet", "find", "findFirst", "findOnlyOne", "exists", "notExists", "count" }`
- **Summary:** Specifies filter patterns for methods when the annotation is applied at the type level.
- **Contract:**
  - Specifies filter patterns for methods when the annotation is applied at the type level.
  - <p> Each entry matches when the method name starts with that entry (case-insensitive), or when the entry matches the full method name as a regular expression.
  - </p> <p> This filter is ignored when the annotation is applied at the method level.
  - </p> <p> When the annotation is applied at the type level, methods whose names contain {@code "page"} or {@code "paginate"} (case-insensitive) are always skipped from caching, regardless of this filter.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** array of method name patterns to cache; the default targets common read methods: {@code query} , {@code queryFor} , {@code list} , {@code get} , {@code batchGet} , {@code find} , {@code findFirst} , {@code findOnlyOne} , {@code exists} , {@code notExists} , and {@code count}

### Annotation DaoConfig (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.DaoConfig)
Provides DAO-level configuration options that affect query generation and execution behavior.

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### addLimitForSingleQuery(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean addLimitForSingleQuery() default false`
- **Summary:** Controls whether to automatically add a LIMIT clause (or its database equivalent) to single-result {@link com.landawn.abacus.query.condition.Condition Condition} -based query methods declared by {@code Dao} / {@code CrudDao} , and to the {@code CrudDao} single-value lookups by ID.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> When {@code true} , the framework appends: </p> <ul> <li> {@code LIMIT 1} for {@code exists(Condition)} , {@code findFirst(...)} , the typed single-value {@code queryForBoolean(...)} through {@code queryForBytes(...)} methods, and the {@code queryForSingleValue(...)} / {@code queryForSingleNonNull(...)} variants </li> <li> {@code LIMIT 2} for {@code findOnlyOne(...)} and the {@code queryForUniqueValue(...)} / {@code queryForUniqueNonNull(...)} variants (so duplicates can still be detected) </li> </ul> <p> The single-value {@code queryForXxx} methods get the limit both in their {@code Condition} form and in the {@code CrudDao} form that looks a value up by ID.
  - </p> <p> On SQL Server the limit renders as {@code OFFSET/FETCH} , whose grammar requires an {@code ORDER BY} clause, so this best-effort limit is only added when the supplied condition carries one; conditions without {@code ORDER BY} execute unchanged.
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code @DaoConfig(addLimitForSingleQuery = true) public interface ProductDao extends CrudDao<Product, Long, ProductDao> { // Built-in Condition-based single-result methods receive a limit when needed: // one row for find-first/exists, two rows for duplicate detection in find-only-one.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} to auto-append the LIMIT clause to built-in single-result methods, {@code false} (default) otherwise
##### callGenerateIdForInsertIfIdNotSet(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean callGenerateIdForInsertIfIdNotSet() default false`
- **Summary:** Controls whether to automatically call {@code generateId()} for entity inserts when the ID field is not set or has a default value.
- **Contract:**
  - Controls whether to automatically call {@code generateId()} for entity inserts when the ID field is not set or has a default value.
  - <p> This applies to {@code CrudDao.insert(T entity)} and {@code CrudDao.batchInsert(Collection<T> entities)} methods (including the {@code batchSize} overloads), and to their {@code propNamesToInsert} overloads when the ID property is among the properties to insert.
  - The ID is considered "not set" when it's null or has the default value for its type (0 for numeric types, {@code null} for objects).
  - </p> <p> The DAO must override {@code generateId()} : the inherited default implementation throws {@code UnsupportedOperationException} , so with this flag enabled an insert of an entity whose ID is not set fails with that exception.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} to auto-generate IDs for insert operations
##### callGenerateIdForInsertWithSqlIfIdNotSet(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean callGenerateIdForInsertWithSqlIfIdNotSet() default false`
- **Summary:** Controls whether to automatically call {@code generateId()} for SQL-based entity inserts when the ID field is not set or has a default value.
- **Contract:**
  - Controls whether to automatically call {@code generateId()} for SQL-based entity inserts when the ID field is not set or has a default value.
  - Similar to {@link #callGenerateIdForInsertIfIdNotSet()} but for custom SQL inserts; the DAO must likewise override {@code generateId()} , whose inherited default implementation throws {@code UnsupportedOperationException} .
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code @DaoConfig(callGenerateIdForInsertWithSqlIfIdNotSet = true) public interface OrderDao extends CrudDao<Order, Long, OrderDao> { @Override default Long generateId() { return System.currentTimeMillis(); } default void insertWithAudit(Order order) throws SQLException { String sql = "INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, total, created_by) " + "VALUES (:id, :customerId, :total, CURRENT_USER())"; insert(sql, order); // generateId() called if order.id not set } } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} to auto-generate IDs for SQL-based insert operations
##### allowNullOrDefaultJoinKeys(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean allowNullOrDefaultJoinKeys() default false`
- **Summary:** Controls whether framework-managed join operations (driven by {@code @JoinedBy} entity annotations) can be performed when the join key value is {@code null} or the type's default value.
- **Contract:**
  - Controls whether framework-managed join operations (driven by {@code @JoinedBy} entity annotations) can be performed when the join key value is {@code null} or the type's default value.
  - When {@code false} (default), an {@code IllegalArgumentException} is thrown at runtime if a {@code null} or default join key is encountered.
  - When {@code true} , the join query is executed with the null/default key instead of raising an error.
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code @DaoConfig(allowNullOrDefaultJoinKeys = true) public interface CustomerDao extends CrudDao<Customer, Long, CustomerDao>, CrudJoinEntityHelper<Customer, Long, CustomerDao> { // @JoinedBy-driven joins are allowed even if the join key is null or zero: // loadJoinEntities/loadAllJoinEntities are inherited from CrudJoinEntityHelper.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} to allow framework-managed joins when join key values are {@code null} or default; {@code false} (default) to throw an exception in that case
##### fetchColumnByEntityClassForDatasetQuery(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean fetchColumnByEntityClassForDatasetQuery() default true`
- **Summary:** Controls the default column-value typing of built-in {@code Dataset} -returning methods (e.g., {@code query(Condition)} , {@code query(Collection<String>, Condition)} ) provided by {@code Dao} / {@code CrudDao} , when the method itself does not override it with {@link FetchColumnByEntityClass @FetchColumnByEntityClass} .
- **Contract:**
  - Controls the default column-value typing of built-in {@code Dataset} -returning methods (e.g., {@code query(Condition)} , {@code query(Collection<String>, Condition)} ) provided by {@code Dao} / {@code CrudDao} , when the method itself does not override it with {@link FetchColumnByEntityClass @FetchColumnByEntityClass} .
  - <p> When {@code true} (default), columns whose labels match properties of the DAO's target entity class are read with those properties' types.
  - When {@code false} , every column is read with the default column-value mapping.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} (default) to read entity-mapped columns with the entity property types; {@code false} to read every column with the default column-value mapping

- **Summary:** Specifies whether column values are read using the property types of the entity class.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> When {@code true} (default): </p> <ul> <li> Columns that match entity properties are read with those properties' types </li> <li> Columns without a matching property are still returned, read with the default mapping </li> <li> {@link PrefixFieldMapping @PrefixFieldMapping} can resolve prefixed column labels to nested properties </li> </ul> <p> When {@code false} : </p> <ul> <li> Every column is read with the default column-value mapping </li> <li> {@link PrefixFieldMapping @PrefixFieldMapping} is not supported </li> </ul> <p> In both cases the {@code Dataset} contains every column produced by the SQL, under its SQL column label.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} to read entity-mapped columns with the entity property types, {@code false} to use the default column-value mapping for every column; defaults to {@code true} , and a value declared here overrides the DAO-level {@link DaoConfig#fetchColumnByEntityClassForDatasetQuery()} default

### Annotation Handler (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.Handler)
Defines an interceptor handler for DAO methods or entire DAO interfaces.

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### qualifier(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `String qualifier() default ""`
- **Summary:** Specifies a qualifier used to look up a pre-registered handler instance: the name of a {@code static final} {@link Jdbc.Handler} field declared in the DAO interface, one of its super-interfaces, or their nested classes, or the qualifier of a handler registered with {@code Jdbc.HandlerFactory} (which, when Spring is available, also finds a {@code Jdbc.Handler} Spring bean of that name).
- **Contract:**
  - Specifies a qualifier used to look up a pre-registered handler instance: the name of a {@code static final} {@link Jdbc.Handler} field declared in the DAO interface, one of its super-interfaces, or their nested classes, or the qualifier of a handler registered with {@code Jdbc.HandlerFactory} (which, when Spring is available, also finds a {@code Jdbc.Handler} Spring bean of that name).
  - When non-empty, the qualifier takes precedence over {@link #impl()} ; the framework resolves the handler by this name instead of instantiating one from the {@code impl} attribute.
  - <p> This is useful when you want to register a handler instance once (with custom configuration or dependencies) and then reference it from multiple DAO interfaces or methods by name.
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code // Register handler instances at startup (e.g., Jdbc.HandlerFactory.register("auditHandler", new AuditHandler(...))) @Handler(qualifier = "auditHandler") public interface ConfigDao extends CrudDao<Config, Long, ConfigDao> { // The handler registered under "auditHandler" will be applied } } </pre> <p> The qualifier must resolve to a handler instance at DAO initialization time: a {@code static final} field of that name on the DAO, its super-interfaces or their nested classes is looked up first, then {@code Jdbc.HandlerFactory} .
  - If neither yields a handler, DAO initialization fails with {@code IllegalArgumentException} .
  - </p> <p> Those {@link Jdbc.Handler} -typed fields are collected whether or not any qualifier references them, and each must be {@code static final} (automatic for an interface field, but not for one declared in a nested class) with a name unique across the DAO, its super-interfaces and their nested classes; violating either rule also fails DAO initialization with {@code IllegalArgumentException} .
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the handler qualifier name; empty (default) means resolve a handler by {@link #impl()} instead
##### impl(...) -> Class<? extends Jdbc.Handler<? extends DaoBase>>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") Class<? extends Jdbc.Handler<? extends DaoBase>> impl() default EmptyHandler.class`
- **Summary:** Specifies the handler implementation class.
- **Contract:**
  - The class must implement {@link Jdbc.Handler} with the appropriate DAO type parameter: the proxy is passed to its typed {@code beforeInvoke} / {@code afterInvoke} methods, so a handler typed for one DAO interface fails with {@code ClassCastException} when applied to another DAO type.
  - A handler shared by several DAO types should be typed for a common supertype such as {@code DaoBase<?, ?>} .
  - If no instance is already registered, the class must be concrete and have a usable no-argument constructor; invalid construction requirements fail with {@code IllegalArgumentException} , while constructor or reflective-access failures can propagate other runtime exceptions.
  - It runs only if this handler's {@code beforeInvoke()} completed normally, including when a later handler's {@code beforeInvoke()} fails.
  - </li> </ol> <p> When the invocation or a {@code beforeInvoke()} call fails, that failure remains primary while distinct {@code afterInvoke()} failures are attached as suppressed exceptions.
  - </p> <p> Example handler implementation: </p> <pre> {@code public class SecurityHandler implements Jdbc.Handler<UserDao> { @Override public void beforeInvoke(UserDao proxy, Object\[\] args, Tuple3<Method, ImmutableList<Class<?>>, Class<?>> methodSignature) { // Check user permissions if (!hasPermission(methodSignature._1)) { throw new SecurityException("Access denied"); } } @Override public void afterInvoke(Object result, UserDao proxy, Object\[\] args, Tuple3<Method, ImmutableList<Class<?>>, Class<?>> methodSignature) { // Can filter or log results filterSensitiveData(result); } } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the handler class, defaults to {@link EmptyHandler} (no-op)
##### filter(...) -> String\[\]
- **Signature:** `String[] filter() default { ".*" }`
- **Summary:** Specifies filter patterns for methods when the annotation is applied at the class level.
- **Contract:**
  - Specifies filter patterns for methods when the annotation is applied at the class level.
  - <p> Each entry matches when the method name starts with that entry (case-insensitive) or when the entry matches the full method name as a regular expression.
  - Multiple patterns are combined with OR logic \\u2014 a method is intercepted if it matches at least one entry.
  - </p> <p> This filter is ignored when the annotation is applied at the method level.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** array of filter patterns (default matches all methods)
##### externalCallsOnly(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean externalCallsOnly() default false`
- **Summary:** Specifies whether this handler should only be applied to external invocations of the DAO.
- **Contract:**
  - Specifies whether this handler should only be applied to external invocations of the DAO.
  - When {@code true} , the handler will not be triggered for internal method calls within the DAO.
  - <p> This is useful for handlers that should only apply when the DAO is called from outside code, not when DAO methods call each other internally.
  - </p> <p> More precisely, a call counts as internal when it is made on the same thread while another DAO method that has at least one {@code @Handler} applied is still executing &mdash; on this DAO or on any other DAO proxy.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** {@code true} if handler only applies to external calls, {@code false} (default) otherwise

### Annotation Handlers (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.Handlers)
Container annotation for multiple {@link Handler} declarations on the same DAO method or type.

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### value(...) -> Handler\[\]
- **Signature:** `Handler[] value()`
- **Summary:** Returns the array of {@link Handler} annotations contained in this list.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> When multiple handlers are applied to a DAO or method, they form a chain of interceptors.
  - </li> </ul> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code // Accessing Handlers programmatically via reflection Handlers handlers = MyDao.class.getAnnotation(Handlers.class); if (handlers != null) { for (Handler handler : handlers.value()) { System.out.println("Handler impl: " + handler.impl()); System.out.println("Filter: " + Arrays.toString(handler.filter())); } } // Multiple handlers are automatically wrapped in Handlers @Handler(impl = LoggingHandler.class) @Handler(impl = SecurityHandler.class) @Handler(impl = CacheHandler.class) public interface UserDao extends CrudDao<User, Long, UserDao> { // The compiler wraps these in a Handlers annotation } } </pre> <p> This element is mandatory and has no default value.
  - When the compiler synthesizes the container from repeated {@link Handler @Handler} annotations it populates this array.
  - An explicit container must supply the array, but Java permits it to be empty; an empty container simply installs no handlers.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the array of {@link Handler} annotations contained in this list

### Annotation MappedByKey (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.MappedByKey)
Transforms query results into a Map structure where each result row is keyed by a specified field.

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### value(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `String value() default ""`
- **Summary:** Specifies the target-entity property name to use as the map key.
- **Contract:**
  - </p> <p> If left empty, the framework falls back to the target entity's id property name (the first id property when the entity has a composite id); a DAO whose entity has no id property then fails initialization with {@code IllegalArgumentException} .
  - </p> <p> The resolved name must be a readable property of the DAO's target entity class, and the method's key type must accept that property's type; otherwise DAO initialization fails with {@code IllegalArgumentException} .
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the field name to use as map key, or empty string to fall back to the entity's id property
##### mapClass(...) -> Class<? extends Map>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") Class<? extends Map> mapClass() default HashMap.class`
- **Summary:** Specifies the Map implementation class to use for the result.
- **Contract:**
  - The class must be concrete, have a no-argument constructor, and be assignable to the DAO method's declared return type; each of those is checked at DAO initialization time and a violation fails with {@code IllegalArgumentException} .
  - For example, a method returning {@code LinkedHashMap} must explicitly select {@code LinkedHashMap.class} ; the default {@link HashMap} is only compatible with return types that can accept a {@code HashMap} , such as {@code Map} or {@code HashMap} .
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the {@code Map} implementation class to instantiate; defaults to {@link HashMap}

### Annotation MergedById (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.MergedById)
Merges multiple result rows into single entities based on ID fields.

**Modifiers:** `public`

#### Public Constructors

- (none)

##### value(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `String value() default ""`
- **Summary:** Specifies the property name(s) whose values identify rows to merge.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> This is optional when merging by the entity's declared id: left empty, the framework falls back to {@link MappedByKey} 's key when the two are combined, and otherwise to the target entity's id property names (those annotated with {@code @Id} , or, when none is, a conventional property named {@code id} ).
  - </p> <p> When {@code @MergedById} and {@link MappedByKey} are combined, an explicit {@code @MergedById} value must name exactly the single property that {@code @MappedByKey} resolves to (its explicit value, or the entity's first id property when that value is empty); otherwise DAO initialization fails with {@code IllegalArgumentException} .
- **Parameters:**

### Annotation OutParameter (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.OutParameter)
Declares an {@code OUT} or {@code INOUT} parameter for a stored-procedure DAO method.

**Modifiers:** `public`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### name(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `String name() default ""`
- **Summary:** Specifies the name of the output parameter.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> Exactly one of {@code name} or {@code position} must be specified for a given {@code @OutParameter} ; supplying both, or neither, fails with {@code UnsupportedOperationException} at DAO initialization time.
  - Named parameters are generally preferred for readability and maintainability when the JDBC driver and procedure support them.
  - </p> <p> The parameter name should match the name used in the stored procedure call syntax.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the parameter name; empty string when {@link #position()} is used instead
- **See also:** CallableStatement#registerOutParameter(String, int)
##### position(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `int position() default -1`
- **Summary:** Specifies the position of the output parameter.
- **Contract:**
  - Exactly one of {@code name} or {@code position} must be specified for a given {@code @OutParameter} (supplying both, or neither, fails with {@code UnsupportedOperationException} at DAO initialization time).
  - In positional procedure SQL the method's arguments (no {@code @Bind} , no {@code Map} ) are bound to positions {@code 1..n} in method-parameter order, so every OUT-only position must come after all IN positions (an INOUT parameter takes its input from the argument bound at its position).
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the parameter position (1-based); {@code -1} (default) when {@link #name()} is used instead
- **See also:** CallableStatement#registerOutParameter(int, int)
##### sqlType(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `int sqlType()`
- **Summary:** Specifies the SQL type of the output parameter.
- **Contract:**
  - The framework forwards the value unchanged, so a vendor-specific integer type code may also be used when the JDBC driver supports it.
  - <p> Common SQL types include: </p> <ul> <li> {@link Types#VARCHAR} - String values </li> <li> {@link Types#INTEGER} - Integer values </li> <li> {@link Types#DECIMAL} or {@link Types#NUMERIC} - Decimal numbers </li> <li> {@link Types#DATE} , {@link Types#TIME} , {@link Types#TIMESTAMP} - Date/time values </li> <li> {@link Types#BOOLEAN} - Boolean values </li> <li> {@link Types#CLOB} - Character large objects </li> <li> {@link Types#BLOB} - Binary large objects </li> </ul> <p> The SQL type must match the actual type of the output parameter in the stored procedure.
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code @OutParameter(name = "message", sqlType = Types.VARCHAR) @OutParameter(name = "count", sqlType = Types.INTEGER) @OutParameter(name = "amount", sqlType = Types.DECIMAL) @OutParameter(name = "processDate", sqlType = Types.TIMESTAMP) @OutParameter(name = "isActive", sqlType = Types.BOOLEAN) } </pre> <p> This element has no default value and must be specified for every {@code @OutParameter} .
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the SQL type code, normally a constant from {@link java.sql.Types}
- **See also:** Types
