##### upsert(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `default T upsert(final T entity, final Collection<String> matchPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Executes an upsert operation: inserts the entity if no record matches the unique properties, otherwise updates the existing record.
- **Contract:**
  - Executes an upsert operation: inserts the entity if no record matches the unique properties, otherwise updates the existing record.
  - </p> <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code User user = new User("john@example.com", "John Doe"); User saved = dao.upsert(user, Arrays.asList("email")); // Inserts if email doesn't exist, updates if it does } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to insert or update
  - `matchPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — property names that uniquely identify the record (a spelling the entity's property lookup accepts, such as the column name, is resolved to the property name)
- **Returns:** the saved entity (the input entity if it was newly inserted; otherwise the merged existing entity that was updated)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} is {@code null} or {@code matchPropNames} is {@code null} or empty, or if any name in {@code matchPropNames} is not a readable property of the entity class (a nested property path such as {@code "address.street"} is not accepted), or an existing row is updated, {@code entity} has ID properties and a non-ID property the loaded entity does not
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in (see {@link #upsert(Object, Condition)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if direct (non-Spring) acquisition of a required database connection fails, or starting or completing the transaction scope (inside a transaction), or telling whether a transaction is active (from the auto-commit mode of a Spring-bound connection), fails. Spring acquisition failures instead propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} .
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if looking up an existing row or executing the required INSERT or UPDATE statement fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one record matches the specified {@code matchPropNames}
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if an existing row is updated and the loaded class is an immutable bean
- **See also:** #upsert(Object, Condition)
- **Signature:** `default T upsert(final T entity, final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Executes an upsert operation: inserts the entity if no record matches the condition, otherwise updates the existing record.
- **Contract:**
  - Executes an upsert operation: inserts the entity if no record matches the condition, otherwise updates the existing record.
  - <p> When a record is found, the non- {@code null} non-id properties of {@code entity} are copied into the loaded record before it is updated; a {@code null} property keeps the existing value, so an upsert cannot clear a column to {@code NULL} .
  - When the input has no ID properties, properties absent from the loaded entity are ignored, and the update addresses the row by {@code cond} .
  - With ID properties, an unmatched non-ID property is rejected, and the update never assigns the ID columns: it addresses the row by its loaded ID values, or, if one of them is {@code null} , by {@code cond} , since a nullable ID need not be unique.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to insert or update
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — condition to check for existence
- **Returns:** the saved entity (the input entity if it was newly inserted; otherwise the merged existing entity that was updated)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} or {@code cond} is {@code null} , or an existing row is updated and {@code entity} has ID properties and a non-ID property the loaded entity does not
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required for the transaction scope the lookup and the write run in there), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if direct (non-Spring) acquisition of a required database connection fails, or starting or completing the transaction scope (inside a transaction), or telling whether a transaction is active (from the auto-commit mode of a Spring-bound connection), fails. Spring acquisition failures instead propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} .
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if looking up an existing row or executing the required INSERT or UPDATE statement fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one record matches the specified condition
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if an existing row is updated and the loaded class is an immutable bean

### Interface DaoBase (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.dao.DaoBase)
Infrastructure root of the DAO capability hierarchy: the shared accessors ( {@code dataSource()} , {@code sqlMapper()} , {@code targetEntityClass()} , {@code targetTableName()} , {@code executor()} ) and the {@code prepareQuery} / {@code prepareNamedQuery} statement builders that every read and write capability relies on.

**Modifiers:** `public sealed`
**Permits:** `ReadOps`, `InsertOps`, `UpdateOps`, `DeleteOps`, `UncheckedDaoBase`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### dataSource(...) -> javax.sql.DataSource
- **Signature:** `@NonDBOperation javax.sql.DataSource dataSource()`
- **Summary:** Retrieves the underlying data source used by this DAO for database connections.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> A DAO interface may override this method with a {@code default} method, for example to route its statements to another data source: the DAO's statements and join operations then use the data source it returns, and so do its transaction checks (the result caches kept out of transactions, the generated IDs put back when a transaction rolls back).
  - It must return a data source of the same database as the one the DAO was created with (the same product and version, and the same schema): the DAO's SQL, its dialect handling, its type mappings and the metadata of its join properties are built from that one, once, when the DAO is created.
  - </p> <p> The selected source must remain consistent throughout each DAO method invocation: transaction and cache checks, statement creation, and join resolution must all observe the same source.
  - Routing metadata uses weak references so that it does not keep retired data sources alive; live data sources retain stable cache namespaces when the route changes and later returns to them.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the data source configured for this DAO
##### sqlMapper(...) -> SqlMapper
- **Signature:** `@NonDBOperation SqlMapper sqlMapper()`
- **Summary:** Retrieves the {@code SqlMapper} instance of this DAO.
- **Contract:**
  - It is this DAO's own copy of the SqlMapper supplied when the DAO was created (a new, empty one if none was supplied), with the SQL loaded from any {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.SqlSource @SqlSource} on the DAO interface or its super-interfaces, and the SQL of the {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.SqlScript @SqlScript} fields of those interfaces and of their directly nested classes, added; later changes to the supplied SqlMapper are not seen by this DAO.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the SqlMapper instance, never {@code null}

##### callAsync(...) -> ContinuableFuture<R>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation") @Beta @NonDBOperation default <R> ContinuableFuture<R> callAsync(final Throwables.Function<? super TD, ? extends R, SQLException> sqlAction) throws IllegalArgumentException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Executes an asynchronous database operation using the default executor.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code ContinuableFuture<List<User>> future = dao.callAsync(d -> d.list(Filters.eq("status", "ACTIVE")) ); ContinuableFuture<Void> printFuture = future.thenRunAsync(users -> users.forEach(System.out::println) ); printFuture.get(); } </pre> <p> Exceptions thrown by {@code sqlAction} , including {@link SQLException} , are retained by the returned future and reported when its result is retrieved.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sqlAction` (`Throwables.Function<? super TD, ? extends R, SQLException>`) — function that performs database operations
- **Returns:** ContinuableFuture with the operation result
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code sqlAction} is {@code null}
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the executor rejects the submitted action
- **Signature:** `@Beta @NonDBOperation default <R> ContinuableFuture<R> callAsync(final Throwables.Function<? super TD, ? extends R, SQLException> sqlAction, final Executor executor) throws IllegalArgumentException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Executes an asynchronous database operation using the specified executor.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService customExecutor = java.util.concurrent.Executors.newFixedThreadPool(10); try { ContinuableFuture<Boolean> future = dao.callAsync( d -> d.exists(Filters.eq("status", "PENDING")), customExecutor ); boolean pendingExists = future.get(); } finally { customExecutor.shutdown(); } } </pre> <p> Exceptions thrown by {@code sqlAction} , including {@link SQLException} , are retained by the returned future and reported when its result is retrieved.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sqlAction` (`Throwables.Function<? super TD, ? extends R, SQLException>`) — function that performs database operations
  - `executor` (`Executor`) — the executor to run the operation
- **Returns:** ContinuableFuture with the operation result
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code sqlAction} or {@code executor} is {@code null}
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the executor rejects the submitted action
##### runAsync(...) -> ContinuableFuture<Void>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation") @Beta @NonDBOperation default ContinuableFuture<Void> runAsync(final Throwables.Consumer<? super TD, SQLException> sqlAction) throws IllegalArgumentException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Executes an asynchronous database operation without a result value using the default executor.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned future should still be observed so database failures are not silently discarded.
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code ContinuableFuture<Void> future = dao.runAsync(d -> { List<User> stale = d.list(Filters.lt("lastAccess", sixMonthsAgo)); System.out.println("stale accounts: " + stale.size()); }); future.get(); } </pre> <p> Exceptions thrown by {@code sqlAction} , including {@link SQLException} , are retained by the returned future and reported when its result is retrieved.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sqlAction` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super TD, SQLException>`) — consumer that performs database operations
- **Returns:** ContinuableFuture that completes when operation finishes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code sqlAction} is {@code null}
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the executor rejects the submitted action
- **Signature:** `@Beta @NonDBOperation default ContinuableFuture<Void> runAsync(final Throwables.Consumer<? super TD, SQLException> sqlAction, final Executor executor) throws IllegalArgumentException, RejectedExecutionException`
- **Summary:** Executes an asynchronous database operation without return value using specified executor.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code java.util.concurrent.ScheduledExecutorService scheduler = java.util.concurrent.Executors.newScheduledThreadPool(5); try { ContinuableFuture<Void> reportFuture = dao.runAsync( d -> { long highValue = d.list(Filters.gt("amount", 1000)).size(); System.out.println("high-value rows: " + highValue); }, scheduler ).thenRunAsync(() -> System.out.println("Report generated") ); reportFuture.get(); } finally { scheduler.shutdown(); } } </pre> <p> Exceptions thrown by {@code sqlAction} , including {@link SQLException} , are retained by the returned future and reported when its result is retrieved.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sqlAction` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super TD, SQLException>`) — consumer that performs database operations
  - `executor` (`Executor`) — the executor to run the operation
- **Returns:** ContinuableFuture that completes when operation finishes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code sqlAction} or {@code executor} is {@code null}
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if the executor rejects the submitted action

##### batchSave(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `default void batchSave(final Collection<? extends T> entities) throws IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Batch saves (inserts) multiple entities using the default batch size.
- **Contract:**
  - As with {@link #save(Object)} , the ID column is included for an entity only when its ID is set.
  - Does nothing if {@code entities} is {@code null} or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the collection of entities to insert
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required when more than one element opens a transaction scope), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a required database connection outside Spring fails, or starting or completing an internally required transaction fails; on the Spring path, acquisition failures propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException}
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if preparing, binding, or executing an INSERT statement fails
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a batch row is {@code null} and the SQL has other than one parameter, or a batch entity lacks a property required by the named SQL parameters
- **See also:** #batchSave(Collection, int)
- **Signature:** `void batchSave(final Collection<? extends T> entities, final int batchSize) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException`
- **Summary:** Batch saves (inserts) multiple entities with a specified batch size.
- **Contract:**

  - Does nothing if {@code entities} is {@code null} or empty.

  - `batchSize` (`int`) — the number of entities to process in each batch. The operation will split large collections into chunks of this size for optimal performance. With more than one element, all of them run in one transaction, even if they fit in one batch.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code batchSize} is not positive, if a batch row is {@code null} and the SQL has other than one parameter, or a batch entity lacks a property required by the named SQL parameters

##### deleteJoinEntities(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `default int deleteJoinEntities(final T entity, final Class<?> joinEntityClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Deletes all join entities of the specified type for a single entity.
- **Contract:**
  - If multiple properties in the entity class are joined to the specified type, all of them are deleted within a single transaction.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity for which to delete join entities
  - `joinEntityClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class of the join entities to delete
- **Returns:** the total number of deleted records
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} or {@code joinEntityClass} is {@code null} , or if no join property of the specified type is found in the entity class, or a join being deleted has a disallowed null/default key
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required when more than one join property opens a transaction scope), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a required database connection fails outside Spring or through an unchecked DAO that translates SQL causes, or starting or completing an internally required transaction fails; untranslated Spring acquisition failures propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException}
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if preparing, binding, or executing a DELETE statement fails
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the total deleted-row count overflows an {@code int}
- **Signature:** `default int deleteJoinEntities(final Collection<T> entities, final Class<?> joinEntityClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Deletes all join entities of the specified type for a collection of entities.
- **Contract:**
  - If multiple properties in the entity class are joined to the specified type, all of them are deleted within a single transaction.
  - If {@code entities} is {@code null} or empty, this method returns 0 without executing a DELETE statement.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<T>`) — the collection of entities for which to delete join entities. If {@code null} or empty, this method returns 0 without executing a DELETE statement
  - `joinEntityClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class of the join entities to delete
- **Returns:** the total number of deleted records
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code joinEntityClass} is {@code null} , or if {@code entities} is not empty and no join property of the specified type is found in the entity class, or a join being deleted has a disallowed null/default key, or if a {@code null} entity is encountered while reading its join keys or properties
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required when more than one entity or join property opens a transaction scope), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a required database connection fails outside Spring or through an unchecked DAO that translates SQL causes, or starting or completing an internally required transaction fails; untranslated Spring acquisition failures propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException}
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if preparing, binding, or executing a DELETE statement fails

- **Signature:** `int deleteJoinEntities(final Collection<T> entities, final String joinEntityPropName) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Deletes join entities for a collection of entities by property name.
- **Contract:**
  - The property name must correspond to a field annotated with {@code @JoinedBy} .
  - When more than one entity is given, all of these DELETE statements are executed within a single transaction.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<T>`) — the collection of entities for which to delete join entities. If {@code null} or empty, this method returns 0 without executing a DELETE statement
  - `joinEntityPropName` (`String`) — the property name of the join entities to delete. Must be a valid property name that exists in the entity class and is annotated with {@code @JoinedBy}
- **Returns:** the total number of deleted records across all parent entities. Returns 0 if no matching records were found or if {@code entities} is {@code null} or empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code joinEntityPropName} is {@code null} or empty, or does not exist or is not properly annotated with {@code @JoinedBy} , or a join being deleted has a disallowed null/default key, or if a {@code null} entity is encountered while reading its join keys or properties
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required when more than one entity opens a transaction scope), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )

  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if preparing, binding, or executing a DELETE statement fails
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the total deleted-row count overflows an {@code int}
- **Performance:** </p> <p> Performance characteristics: </p> <ul> <li> For N parent entities, executes O(1) or O(N / batch size) DELETE statements instead of O(N) </li> <li> Much more efficient than deleting join entities one parent at a time </li> <li> The actual number of deleted records may be less than or greater than the number of parent entities </li> </ul> <p> Important notes: </p> <ul> <li> This operation does NOT modify the in-memory join properties of the entities </li> <li> All deletions are permanent unless executed within a transaction </li> <li> For a many-to-many join (through an intermediate entity), the referenced entity rows themselves are deleted, located through the intermediate table; the intermediate-table rows are not deleted by this method and are expected to be removed by the database, e.g.

  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required when more than one entity or join property opens a transaction scope), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if parallel execution is requested and the executor rejects a join task
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedInterruptedException` — if the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for the parallel delete tasks to finish
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if, inside a transaction, beginning or completing the scope the deletes of several properties run in fails (see {@link #deleteJoinEntities(Collection, Collection)} )
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if acquiring a database connection, starting or completing an internally required transaction, or preparing, binding, or executing a DELETE statement fails in a delete task
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the total deleted-row count overflows an {@code int}

##### joinTaskExecutor(...) -> Executor
- **Signature:** `static Executor joinTaskExecutor(final JoinEntityBase<?, ?> dao, final Executor executor)`
- **Summary:** Returns the executor that the parallel join load tasks of {@code dao} run with: {@code executor} , or the calling thread itself while it runs a transaction on the DAO's data source (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#isInTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} ; also when that can't be determined).
- **Contract:**
  - Returns the executor that the parallel join load tasks of {@code dao} run with: {@code executor} , or the calling thread itself while it runs a transaction on the DAO's data source (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#isInTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} ; also when that can't be determined).
- **Parameters:**
  - `dao` (`JoinEntityBase<?, ?>`) — the DAO the join tasks run on
  - `executor` (`Executor`) — the executor requested for the join tasks
- **Returns:** the executor to run them with
##### isInTransaction(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `static boolean isInTransaction(final JoinEntityBase<?, ?> dao)`
- **Summary:** Returns whether the calling thread runs in a transaction on the data source of {@code dao} (see {@link JdbcUtil#isInTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} ), the join tasks of a parallel load or delete then running on it, in the transaction (see {@link #joinTaskExecutor(JoinEntityBase, Executor)} for the loads; the deletes then run as their sequential overloads do).
- **Parameters:**
  - `dao` (`JoinEntityBase<?, ?>`) — the DAO the join tasks run on
- **Returns:** {@code true} if it does, or if that can't be determined (the calling thread is always a safe choice)
##### checkJoinEntityPropNames(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation") static void checkJoinEntityPropNames(final JoinEntityBase<?, ?> dao, final Collection<String> joinEntityPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Checks that every name in {@code joinEntityPropNames} names a join entity property of the DAO's entity class (one annotated with {@code @JoinedBy} ), before the join loads and deletes of several names run any: an invalid name failed only once the names before it had been loaded or deleted, in its own task for the executor-based ones (so a parallel delete outside a transaction committed the deletes of the valid names before throwing), and, for a sequential delete, inside the scope the deletes run in, which then marked the caller's transaction rollback-only.
- **Parameters:**
  - `dao` (`JoinEntityBase<?, ?>`) — the DAO the joins are loaded or deleted through
  - `joinEntityPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a name is {@code null} or empty, or names no join entity property
##### checkJoinEntityPropNamesIfAbsent(...) -> List<String>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation") static List<String> checkJoinEntityPropNamesIfAbsent(final JoinEntityBase<?, ?> dao, final Collection<?> entities, final Collection<String> joinEntityPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** As {@link #checkJoinEntityPropNames(JoinEntityBase, Collection)} , for the {@code loadJoinEntitiesIfAbsent} of several names, with the rules, the order and the exceptions of the single-name overloads, name by name: no element of {@code entities} may be {@code null} , every name must be non-empty and name a property of the entity class (the class of the first element), and one that is {@code null} on at least one entity must be a join entity property.
- **Contract:**
  - As {@link #checkJoinEntityPropNames(JoinEntityBase, Collection)} , for the {@code loadJoinEntitiesIfAbsent} of several names, with the rules, the order and the exceptions of the single-name overloads, name by name: no element of {@code entities} may be {@code null} , every name must be non-empty and name a property of the entity class (the class of the first element), and one that is {@code null} on at least one entity must be a join entity property.
- **Parameters:**
  - `dao` (`JoinEntityBase<?, ?>`) — the DAO the joins are loaded through
  - `entities` (`Collection<?>`) — the entities, not empty
  - `joinEntityPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names
- **Returns:** the names whose property is {@code null} on at least one entity, in order: the ones to load
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if an element of {@code entities} is {@code null} , or a name breaks these rules
##### submitJoinTasks(...) -> List<ContinuableFuture<R>>
- **Signature:** `static <R> List<ContinuableFuture<R>> submitJoinTasks(final Collection<String> joinEntityPropNames, final Function<? super String, ContinuableFuture<R>> taskSubmitter)`
- **Summary:** Submits one parallel join task per property name, as used by the executor-based join load/delete methods.
- **Contract:**
  - If submitting a task fails (typically a {@link RejectedExecutionException} from a saturated or shut-down executor), the tasks already submitted are awaited before that failure is rethrown, with their failures attached as suppressed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `joinEntityPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the join property names, one task per name
  - `taskSubmitter` (`Function<? super String, ContinuableFuture<R>>`) — submits the task for one property name to the executor
- **Returns:** the futures of all submitted tasks, in iteration order of {@code joinEntityPropNames}

##### findFirst(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `default Optional<T> findFirst(final Collection<String> sourceSelectPropNames, final Class<?> joinEntityClass, final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Finds the first entity that matches the specified condition and loads the specified type of join entities.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceSelectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the properties (columns) to be selected from the main entity, excluding join entity properties. If {@code null} , all properties of the main entity are selected
  - `joinEntityClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class of the join entities to load
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition to match
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the entity with join entities loaded, or empty if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code joinEntityClass} or {@code cond} is {@code null} , or a matching entity is found and no join property of the specified type exists in the entity class, or a join being loaded has a disallowed null/default key or multiple rows for a map-valued property
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a required database connection fails outside Spring or through an unchecked DAO that translates SQL causes; untranslated Spring acquisition failures propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException}
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if preparing or executing the SELECT statement, binding its parameters, or reading its result fails
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a join property being loaded is read-only

##### stream(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta default Stream<T> stream(final Collection<String> sourceSelectPropNames, final Class<?> joinEntityClass, final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Streams entities that match the specified condition and loads the specified type of join entities for each.
- **Contract:**
  - Any {@link SQLException} thrown while loading join entities during stream consumption is wrapped as an {@link UncheckedSQLException} ; if no join property of the specified type is found, an {@link IllegalArgumentException} is thrown during stream consumption.
  - The driver must support another statement while the parent result remains open; for example, Connector/J's {@code Integer.MIN_VALUE} streaming mode can reject this.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceSelectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the properties (columns) to be selected from the main entity, excluding join entity properties. If {@code null} , all properties of the main entity are selected
  - `joinEntityClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class of the join entities to load
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition to match
- **Returns:** a {@code Stream} of entities matching the condition with join entities loaded
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code joinEntityClass} or {@code cond} is {@code null} , or metadata needed to augment an explicit source selection is invalid
- **Signature:** `@Beta default Stream<T> stream(final Collection<String> sourceSelectPropNames, final Collection<Class<?>> joinEntityClasses, final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Streams entities that match the specified condition and loads multiple types of join entities for each.
- **Contract:**
  - Any {@link SQLException} thrown while loading join entities during stream consumption is wrapped as an {@link UncheckedSQLException} ; if no join property is found for one of the specified types, an {@link IllegalArgumentException} is thrown during stream consumption.
  - If {@code joinEntityClasses} is {@code null} or empty, the underlying entity stream is returned unmodified.
  - <p> When join entities are requested, the parent query keeps its connection open while each batch's join queries run.
  - The driver must support another statement while the parent result remains open; for example, Connector/J's {@code Integer.MIN_VALUE} streaming mode can reject this.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceSelectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the properties (columns) to be selected from the main entity, excluding join entity properties. If {@code null} , all properties of the main entity are selected
  - `joinEntityClasses` (`Collection<Class<?>>`) — the collection of join entity classes to load. If {@code null} or empty, no join entities are loaded
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition to match
- **Returns:** a {@code Stream} of entities matching the condition with join entities loaded
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code joinEntityClasses} contains a {@code null} element, or {@code cond} is {@code null} , or metadata needed to augment an explicit source selection is invalid
- **Signature:** `@Beta default Stream<T> stream(final Collection<String> sourceSelectPropNames, final boolean includeAllJoinEntities, final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Streams entities that match the specified condition, optionally loading all join entities.
- **Contract:**
  - When {@code includeAllJoinEntities} is {@code true} , the stream processes entities in batches of {@link JdbcUtil#DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE} for efficient memory usage; any {@link SQLException} thrown while loading join entities during stream consumption is wrapped as an {@link UncheckedSQLException} .
  - When {@code includeAllJoinEntities} is {@code false} , the underlying entity stream is returned without modification.
  - <p> When {@code includeAllJoinEntities} is {@code true} , the parent query keeps its connection open while each batch's join queries run.
  - The driver must support another statement while the parent result remains open; for example, Connector/J's {@code Integer.MIN_VALUE} streaming mode can reject this.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceSelectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the properties (columns) to be selected from the main entity, excluding join entity properties. If {@code null} , all properties of the main entity are selected
  - `includeAllJoinEntities` (`boolean`) — if {@code true} , all join entities will be loaded; if {@code false} , no join entities are loaded
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition to match
- **Returns:** a {@code Stream} of entities matching the condition with join entities loaded as specified
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code cond} is {@code null} , or metadata needed to augment an explicit source selection is invalid

  - If multiple properties in the entity class are joined to the specified type, only those whose value is {@code null} are loaded.

- **Parameters:**

  - `joinEntityClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class of the join entities to load
  - `joinSelectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the properties (columns) to be selected from the join entities. If {@code null} , all properties of the join entities are selected
- **Throws:**

  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a required database connection fails outside Spring or through an unchecked DAO that translates SQL causes; untranslated Spring acquisition failures propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException}
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if selecting or reading the requested joined rows fails
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a join property being loaded is read-only

- **Summary:** Loads multiple join entities for a single entity only if they are currently {@code null} , using a custom executor for parallel execution.
- **Contract:**
  - Loads multiple join entities for a single entity only if they are currently {@code null} , using a custom executor for parallel execution.
  - Every property name is checked before any task is submitted (to be non-empty, to exist in the entity class, and, if the property is currently {@code null} , to be annotated with {@code @JoinedBy} ), so an invalid name fails without starting any load.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity for which to load join entities
  - `joinEntityPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names of the join entities to load. If {@code null} or empty, this method returns immediately
  - `executor` (`Executor`) — the executor to use for parallel loading; not used inside a transaction on the DAO's data source, where the joins are loaded on the calling thread, in the transaction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} or {@code executor} is {@code null} , or if any of the {@code joinEntityPropNames} is {@code null} or empty or does not exist, or names a property that is currently {@code null} and is not annotated with {@code @JoinedBy} , or a join being loaded has a disallowed null/default key or multiple rows for a map-valued property
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if parallel execution is requested and the executor rejects a join task
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if acquiring a database connection, or selecting or reading the requested joined rows, fails in a join task
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a join property being loaded is read-only
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedInterruptedException` — if the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for the parallel join tasks to finish

  - `executor` (`Executor`) — the executor to use for parallel loading; not used inside a transaction on the DAO's data source, where the joins are loaded on the calling thread, in the transaction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code executor} is {@code null} , or a join being loaded has a disallowed null/default key or multiple rows for a map-valued property, or if a {@code null} entity is encountered while reading its join keys or properties
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if parallel execution is requested and the executor rejects a join task
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if acquiring a database connection, or selecting or reading the requested joined rows, fails in a join task
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a join property being loaded is read-only
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedInterruptedException` — if the calling thread is interrupted while waiting for the parallel join tasks to finish

##### exists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean exists(final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException`
- **Summary:** Checks if at least one record exists that matches the specified condition.
- **Contract:**
  - Checks if at least one record exists that matches the specified condition.
  - More efficient than counting when you only need to know if records exist.
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code boolean hasActiveUsers = dao.exists(Filters.eq("status", "ACTIVE")); if (hasActiveUsers) { // Process active users } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition to check
- **Returns:** {@code true} if at least one matching record exists
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code cond} is {@code null}
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if direct (non-Spring) acquisition of a required database connection fails. Spring acquisition failures instead propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} .
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if preparing or executing the SELECT statement, binding its parameters, or reading its result fails
- **See also:** AbstractQuery#exists()
##### notExists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Beta default boolean notExists(final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException`
- **Summary:** Convenience method equivalent to the negation of {@link #exists(Condition)} .
- **Contract:**
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code if (dao.notExists(Filters.eq("email", email))) { // Email is available, proceed with registration } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition to check
- **Returns:** {@code true} if no matching records exist
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code cond} is {@code null}
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if direct (non-Spring) acquisition of a required database connection fails. Spring acquisition failures instead propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} .
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if preparing or executing the SELECT statement, binding its parameters, or reading its result fails
- **See also:** #exists(Condition)

##### queryForBoolean(...) -> OptionalBoolean
- **Signature:** `OptionalBoolean queryForBoolean(final String singleSelectPropName, final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException, SQLException`
- **Summary:** Queries the value of a single boolean column for the first record matching the condition.
- **Contract:**
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code OptionalBoolean isActive = dao.queryForBoolean("is_active", Filters.eq("id", 123)); if (isActive.orElse(false)) { // User is active } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - `singleSelectPropName` (`String`) — the name of the single property/column to select
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the search condition
- **Returns:** an {@code OptionalBoolean} holding the selected value when at least one record matches, or an empty {@code OptionalBoolean} if no record matches the condition. A SQL {@code NULL} value is returned as <i> present </i> holding the primitive default {@code false} ; use {@link #queryForSingleValue(String, Condition, Class)} to distinguish SQL {@code NULL} from a real {@code false} .
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code singleSelectPropName} is {@code null} or empty, or if {@code cond} is {@code null}
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if direct (non-Spring) acquisition of a required database connection fails. Spring acquisition failures instead propagate as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} .
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if preparing or executing the SELECT statement, binding its parameters, or reading its result fails
- **See also:** AbstractQuery#queryForBoolean()

##### paginate(...) -> Stream<Dataset>
- **Signature:** `@Beta @LazyEvaluation Stream<Dataset> paginate(final Condition cond, final int pageSize, final Jdbc.BiParametersSetter<? super PreparedQuery, Dataset> paramSetter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a paginated Stream of query results as Dataset pages.
- **Contract:**
  - The condition must include an {@code orderBy} clause for consistent pagination.
  - The parameter setter must advance the query to the next page; no offset is advanced automatically.
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code try (Stream<Dataset> pages = dao.paginate( Criteria.builder().where(Filters.gt("id", 0)).orderBy("id").build(), 100, (query, lastPageResult) -> { if (lastPageResult != null && lastPageResult.size() > 0) { long lastId = (Long) N.lastOrNullIfEmpty(lastPageResult.getColumn("id")); query.setLong(1, lastId); } } )) { pages.forEach(page -> processPage(page)); } } </pre> <p> Database access and callbacks run during stream consumption.
  - Any {@link SQLException} from preparing or executing a page, setting parameters, or extracting results is wrapped in {@link UncheckedSQLException} when the stream is consumed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition; must include an {@code orderBy} clause for consistent pagination
  - `pageSize` (`int`) — the number of records per page, applied as a {@code LIMIT} ; if {@code cond} already carries its own limit, that limit is kept and {@code pageSize} only sets the fetch size
  - `paramSetter` (`Jdbc.BiParametersSetter<? super PreparedQuery, Dataset>`) — function to set parameters for the next page based on the previous page's result (the second argument is {@code null} when fetching the first page)
- **Returns:** stream of Dataset pages
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code cond} or {@code paramSetter} is {@code null} , {@code pageSize} is not positive, or {@code cond} does not include an {@code orderBy} clause
- **Signature:** `@Beta @LazyEvaluation <R> Stream<R> paginate(final Condition cond, final int pageSize, final Jdbc.BiParametersSetter<? super PreparedQuery, R> paramSetter, final Jdbc.ResultExtractor<? extends R> resultExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a paginated Stream with custom result extraction.
- **Contract:**
  - The parameter setter must advance the query to the next page.
  - Iteration stops when the extractor returns {@code null} or an empty {@code Dataset} , {@code Collection} , {@code Map} , {@code Iterable} , or {@code Iterator} ; that terminating result is not emitted.
  - For any other result type, the extractor must return {@code null} when no rows remain.
  - Any {@link SQLException} from preparing or executing a page, setting parameters, or extracting results is wrapped in {@link UncheckedSQLException} when the stream is consumed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition; must include an {@code orderBy} clause for consistent pagination
  - `pageSize` (`int`) — the number of records per page, applied as a {@code LIMIT} ; if {@code cond} already carries its own limit, that limit is kept and {@code pageSize} only sets the fetch size
  - `paramSetter` (`Jdbc.BiParametersSetter<? super PreparedQuery, R>`) — function to set parameters for the next page based on the previous page's result (the second argument is {@code null} when fetching the first page)
  - `resultExtractor` (`Jdbc.ResultExtractor<? extends R>`) — function to process each page's ResultSet
- **Returns:** stream of processed page results
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code cond} , {@code paramSetter} , or {@code resultExtractor} is {@code null} , {@code pageSize} is not positive, or {@code cond} does not include an {@code orderBy} clause
- **Signature:** `@Beta @LazyEvaluation <R> Stream<R> paginate(final Condition cond, final int pageSize, final Jdbc.BiParametersSetter<? super PreparedQuery, R> paramSetter, final Jdbc.BiResultExtractor<? extends R> resultExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException`

  - `paramSetter` (`Jdbc.BiParametersSetter<? super PreparedQuery, R>`) — function to set parameters for the next page based on the previous page's result (the second argument is {@code null} when fetching the first page)

### Interface UncheckedCrudDao (com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.dao.UncheckedCrudDao)
Provides comprehensive CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations with unchecked exception handling.

**Modifiers:** `public non-sealed`
**Extends:** `UncheckedCrudReadOps<T, ID, TD>`, `UncheckedCrudInsertOps<T, ID, TD>`, `UncheckedCrudUpdateOps<T, ID, TD>`, `UncheckedCrudDeleteOps<T, ID, TD>`, `UncheckedDao<T, TD>`, `CrudDao<T, ID, TD>`
**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### upsert(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@Override default T upsert(final T entity) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Performs an upsert operation, matching existing records by the entity's ID property(ies): inserts {@code entity} if no record with the same ID exists; otherwise updates the existing record with the values from {@code entity} .
- **Contract:**
  - Performs an upsert operation, matching existing records by the entity's ID property(ies): inserts {@code entity} if no record with the same ID exists; otherwise updates the existing record with the values from {@code entity} .
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to insert or update (must not be {@code null} )
- **Returns:** the saved entity (the input entity if it was newly inserted; otherwise the merged existing entity that was updated)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} is {@code null} , or an existing row is updated and {@code entity} has a non-ID property the loaded entity does not
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in (see {@link #upsert(Object, Condition)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, starting or completing the transaction scope (inside a transaction), or telling whether a transaction is active (from the auto-commit mode of a Spring-bound connection), fails, or looking up an existing row or executing the required INSERT or UPDATE statement fails. A Spring acquisition failure of the connection for the INSERT (outside a transaction, when no existing row is found) is not translated and propagates as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} .
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one record matches the entity's ID property(ies)
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if no existing row is found, {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.DaoConfig#callGenerateIdForInsertIfIdNotSet()} is enabled, the entity's ID is not set and {@link #generateId()} has not been overridden; or if an existing row is updated and the loaded class is an immutable bean
- **Signature:** `@Override default T upsert(final T entity, final Collection<String> matchPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Performs an upsert operation, matching existing records by the specified unique properties: inserts {@code entity} if no record with the same values exists; otherwise updates the existing record with the values from {@code entity} .
- **Contract:**
  - Performs an upsert operation, matching existing records by the specified unique properties: inserts {@code entity} if no record with the same values exists; otherwise updates the existing record with the values from {@code entity} .
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to insert or update (must not be {@code null} )
  - `matchPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names that uniquely identify the record (must not be empty) (a spelling the entity's property lookup accepts, such as the column name, is resolved to the property name)
- **Returns:** the saved entity (the input entity if it was newly inserted; otherwise the merged existing entity that was updated)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} is {@code null} or {@code matchPropNames} is {@code null} or empty, or if any name in {@code matchPropNames} is not a readable property of the entity class (a nested property path such as {@code "address.street"} is not accepted), or an existing row is updated and {@code entity} has a non-ID property the loaded entity does not
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in (see {@link #upsert(Object, Condition)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, starting or completing the transaction scope (inside a transaction), or telling whether a transaction is active (from the auto-commit mode of a Spring-bound connection), fails, or looking up an existing row or executing the required INSERT or UPDATE statement fails. A Spring acquisition failure of the connection for the INSERT (outside a transaction, when no existing row is found) is not translated and propagates as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} .
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one record matches the specified {@code matchPropNames}
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if no existing row is found, {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.DaoConfig#callGenerateIdForInsertIfIdNotSet()} is enabled, the entity's ID is not set and {@link #generateId()} has not been overridden; or if an existing row is updated and the loaded class is an immutable bean
- **Signature:** `@Override default T upsert(final T entity, final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Performs an upsert operation: inserts {@code entity} if no record matches the specified condition; otherwise copies the non- {@code null} non-id properties from {@code entity} into the existing record (loaded via {@link #findOnlyOne(Condition)} ) and updates it.
- **Contract:**
  - Performs an upsert operation: inserts {@code entity} if no record matches the specified condition; otherwise copies the non- {@code null} non-id properties from {@code entity} into the existing record (loaded via {@link #findOnlyOne(Condition)} ) and updates it.
  - A complete ID addresses the loaded row using its declared database types; if an ID component is {@code null} , the update reuses {@code cond} , since nullable IDs need not be unique.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to insert or update (must not be {@code null} )
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition used to look up an existing record (must not be {@code null} )
- **Returns:** the saved entity: the inserted {@code entity} when no existing record was found, or the loaded database entity (with non- {@code null} non-id properties copied from {@code entity} ) when an existing record was updated
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} or {@code cond} is {@code null} , or an existing row is updated and {@code entity} has a non-ID property the loaded entity does not
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required for the transaction scope the lookup and the write run in there), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, starting or completing the transaction scope (inside a transaction), or telling whether a transaction is active (from the auto-commit mode of a Spring-bound connection), fails, or looking up an existing row or executing the required INSERT or UPDATE statement fails. A Spring acquisition failure of the connection for the INSERT (outside a transaction, when no existing row is found) is not translated and propagates as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} .
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one record matches the specified condition
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if no existing row is found, {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.DaoConfig#callGenerateIdForInsertIfIdNotSet()} is enabled, the entity's ID is not set and {@link #generateId()} has not been overridden; or if an existing row is updated and the loaded class is an immutable bean
- **See also:** Filters

- **Summary:** Performs batch upsert of multiple entities using the default batch size ( {@link JdbcUtil#DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE} ).

- **Signature:** `@Override default List<T> batchUpsert(final Collection<? extends T> entities, final Collection<String> matchPropNames, final int batchSize) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException, IllegalStateException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Performs batch upsert based on the specified unique properties with a custom batch size.
- **Contract:**
  - The lookups and the writes run in one transaction scope inside a transaction, as for {@link #upsert(Object, Condition)} , and, outside one, for more than one entity, as other DAO batch operations do (they used to run apart: the lookups before it, each on a connection of its own, and the writes in a transaction only when both inserts and updates were needed or either set was large); a single entity outside a transaction is upserted as by {@code upsert} .
  - If that transaction, or a transaction enclosing this call, rolls back, the IDs that {@code batchInsert} wrote onto the new entities are put back to their previous values.
  - Inside an active Spring-managed transaction that owns the data source's connection, the transaction participates in it (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} ): Spring commits the work, a failure marks the Spring transaction rollback-only, and the IDs are put back if Spring rolls it back (this needs Spring's transaction synchronization, which is enabled by default, and follows the innermost Spring-managed transaction on the thread, as for {@code insert} ).
  - a component of the primary key, when matching by id) matches no row and is inserted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the collection of entities to upsert
  - `matchPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names that uniquely identify each entity (must not be empty)
  - `batchSize` (`int`) — the number of entities to process in each batch. The operation will split large collections into chunks of this size for optimal performance.

##### insert(...) -> ID
- **Signature:** `@Override ID insert(final T entity) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException`
- **Summary:** Inserts the specified entity into the database and returns its ID.
- **Contract:**
  - All insertable properties of the entity are included in the INSERT statement; the ID property is included only when it has been set (i.e., is not the default value), allowing the database to generate it otherwise.
  - <p> If the database generates the ID (for example via an auto-increment column), the generated ID is retrieved, written back to the entity's ID property (where applicable) and returned.
  - If the database does not generate a key, the entity's existing ID value is returned instead.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to insert (must not be {@code null} )
- **Returns:** the ID of the inserted entity (either database-generated or entity-provided)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} is {@code null}
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation.DaoConfig#callGenerateIdForInsertIfIdNotSet()} is enabled and the entity's ID is not set, but {@link #generateId()} has not been overridden
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the ownership of a Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined (the insert registers the put-back of the entity's ID with a transaction enclosing it)
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if direct (non-Spring) acquisition of a connection fails, if the auto-commit mode of the connection a Spring-managed transaction bound to the data source cannot be read, or preparing, binding, or executing an INSERT statement, or reading its generated keys fails. A Spring acquisition failure is not translated: it propagates as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} (see {@link UncheckedCrudDao} ).

- **Signature:** `@Beta @Override default Optional<T> get(final ID id, final Class<?> joinEntityClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves an entity by its ID and loads the specified type of join entities.
- **Contract:**
  - Only the join properties of the specified class will be loaded; if multiple properties in the entity class are joined to that type, all of them are loaded.
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code // Get user with their orders loaded Optional<User> user = userDao.get(userId, Order.class); if (user.isPresent()) { List<Order> orders = user.get().getOrders(); // Orders are already loaded } } </pre>

- **Signature:** `@Override OptionalBoolean queryForBoolean(final String singleSelectPropName, final ID id) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException`
- **Summary:** Returns an {@code OptionalBoolean} describing the value of a single property for the entity with the specified ID.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns an empty {@code OptionalBoolean} only when no record matches the given id.
  - If a matching record's value is SQL {@code null} , the returned optional is <i> present </i> and holds the primitive default ( {@code false} ); use {@link #queryForSingleValue(String, Object, Class)} to distinguish SQL {@code null} from a real {@code false} .
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code OptionalBoolean isActive = userDao.queryForBoolean("isActive", userId); if (isActive.isPresent() && isActive.getAsBoolean()) { // User is active } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - `singleSelectPropName` (`String`) — the property name to select
  - `id` (`ID`) — the entity ID
- **Returns:** an {@code OptionalBoolean} holding the selected value when a record matches the id (present, holding the primitive default {@code false} when the value is SQL {@code null} ), or an empty {@code OptionalBoolean} when no record matches the id
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code singleSelectPropName} is {@code null} or empty, or if {@code id} is {@code null}

##### refresh(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Beta @Override default boolean refresh(final T entity) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Refreshes the specified entity by reloading all of its (non-join) properties from the database.
- **Contract:**
  - The entity must have its ID set.
  - <p> <b> Usage Examples: </b> </p> <pre> {@code User user = new User(); user.setId(123L); boolean found = userDao.refresh(user); if (found) { // User now contains all current values from database System.out.println("User email: " + user.getEmail()); } } </pre>
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to refresh (must have ID set)
- **Returns:** {@code true} if the entity was found and refreshed, {@code false} if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} is {@code null} , or the entity's single ID value is {@code null}
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, or selecting the current database values or reading the result fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one record matches the entity's id
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a matching database row is found but the entity cannot be written to in place because its class is treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor)
- **Signature:** `@Beta @Override default boolean refresh(final T entity, final Collection<String> propNamesToRefresh) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Refreshes only the specified properties of the entity from the database.
- **Contract:**
  - The entity must have its ID set.
  - Composite IDs are matched using the entity's ID properties, including when the DAO declares a separate bean or record type for the ID.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to refresh (must have ID set)
  - `propNamesToRefresh` (`Collection<String>`) — the properties to refresh from the database
- **Returns:** {@code true} if the matching database row was found and {@code entity} was updated; {@code false} if no matching row exists
- **Throws:**

##### update(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `@Override int update(final T entity) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedSQLException`

- **Returns:** the number of rows updated (typically 1 if successful, 0 if not found); also 0, without executing any statement, if the entity class has no updatable non-ID property

##### batchUpdate(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `@Override default int batchUpdate(final Collection<? extends T> entities) throws IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, ArithmeticException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Batch updates multiple entities using the default batch size ( {@link JdbcUtil#DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE} ).
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the collection of entities to update
- **Returns:** the total number of rows updated (batch entries for which the driver reports {@code Statement.SUCCESS_NO_INFO} contribute 0); 0, without executing any statement, if {@code entities} is {@code null} or empty or the entity class has no updatable non-ID property
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required when more than one element opens a transaction scope), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, starting or completing an internally required transaction fails, or preparing, binding, or executing an UPDATE statement fails. With more than one element, the transaction is begun first and a Spring acquisition failure is not translated: it propagates as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} (see {@link UncheckedDao} )
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the total affected-row count overflows an {@code int}
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a batch row is {@code null} and the SQL has other than one parameter, or a batch entity lacks a property required by the named SQL parameters

  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the total affected-row count overflows an {@code int}

##### upsert(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@Override default T upsert(final T entity, final Collection<String> matchPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Executes an upsert operation: inserts the entity if no record matches the unique properties, otherwise updates the existing record.
- **Contract:**
  - Executes an upsert operation: inserts the entity if no record matches the unique properties, otherwise updates the existing record.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to insert or update
  - `matchPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the list of property names that uniquely identify the record (a spelling the entity's property lookup accepts, such as the column name, is resolved to the property name)
- **Returns:** the saved entity (the input entity if it was newly inserted; otherwise the merged existing entity that was updated)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} is {@code null} or {@code matchPropNames} is {@code null} or empty, or if any name in {@code matchPropNames} is not a readable property of the entity class (a nested property path such as {@code "address.street"} is not accepted), or an existing row is updated, {@code entity} has ID properties and a non-ID property the loaded entity does not
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in (see {@link #upsert(Object, Condition)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, starting or completing the transaction scope (inside a transaction), or telling whether a transaction is active (from the auto-commit mode of a Spring-bound connection), fails, or looking up an existing row or executing the required INSERT or UPDATE statement fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one record matches the specified {@code matchPropNames}
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if an existing row is updated and the loaded class is an immutable bean
- **See also:** #upsert(Object, Condition)
- **Signature:** `@Override default T upsert(final T entity, final Condition cond) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, DuplicateResultException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Executes an upsert operation: inserts the entity if no record matches the condition, otherwise updates the existing record.
- **Contract:**
  - Executes an upsert operation: inserts the entity if no record matches the condition, otherwise updates the existing record.
  - <p> When a record is found, the non- {@code null} non-id properties of {@code entity} are copied into the loaded record before it is updated; a {@code null} property keeps the existing value, so an upsert cannot clear a column to {@code NULL} .
  - When the input has no ID properties, properties absent from the loaded entity are ignored, and the update addresses the row by {@code cond} .
  - With ID properties, an unmatched non-ID property is rejected, and the update never assigns the ID columns: it addresses the row by its loaded ID values, or, if one of them is {@code null} , by {@code cond} , since a nullable ID need not be unique.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity to insert or update
  - `cond` (`Condition`) — the condition to verify if the record exists
- **Returns:** the saved entity (the input entity if it was newly inserted; otherwise the merged existing entity that was updated)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} or {@code cond} is {@code null} , or an existing row is updated and {@code entity} has ID properties and a non-ID property the loaded entity does not
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required for the transaction scope the lookup and the write run in there), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, starting or completing the transaction scope (inside a transaction), or telling whether a transaction is active (from the auto-commit mode of a Spring-bound connection), fails, or looking up an existing row or executing the required INSERT or UPDATE statement fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.DuplicateResultException` — if more than one record matches the specified condition
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if an existing row is updated and the loaded class is an immutable bean

##### batchSave(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override default void batchSave(final Collection<? extends T> entities) throws IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Batch saves (inserts) multiple entities using the default batch size.
- **Contract:**
  - As with {@link #save(Object)} , the ID column is included for an entity only when its ID is set.
  - Does nothing if {@code entities} is {@code null} or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entities` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the collection of entities to insert
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required when more than one element opens a transaction scope), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, starting or completing an internally required transaction fails, or preparing, binding, or executing an INSERT statement fails. With more than one element, the transaction is begun first and a Spring acquisition failure is not translated: it propagates as {@code CannotGetJdbcConnectionException} (see {@link UncheckedDao} )
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a batch row is {@code null} and the SQL has other than one parameter, or a batch entity lacks a property required by the named SQL parameters
- **See also:** #batchSave(Collection, int)

  - `batchSize` (`int`) — the number of entities to process in each batch. The operation will split large collections into chunks of this size for optimal performance. With more than one element, all of them run in one transaction, even if they fit in one batch.

Delete-side view of {@link UncheckedJoinEntityHelper} : the join-entity <i> delete </i> operations ( {@code deleteJoinEntities} / {@code deleteAllJoinEntities} families) that throw {@link UncheckedSQLException} instead of the checked {@link SQLException} .

- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation") @Override default int deleteJoinEntities(final T entity, final Class<?> joinEntityClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UncheckedSQLException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Deletes all join entities of the specified type for a single entity.
- **Contract:**
  - If multiple properties in the entity class are joined to the specified type, all of them are deleted within a single transaction.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`T`) — the entity whose join entities should be deleted
  - `joinEntityClass` (`Class<?>`) — the class of join entities to delete
- **Returns:** the total number of deleted records
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if {@code entity} or {@code joinEntityClass} is {@code null} , or if no join property of the specified type is found in the entity class, or a join being deleted has a disallowed null/default key
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the call runs inside a Spring-managed transaction it cannot participate in: no {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.SpringTransactionTracker} was registered with its transaction manager before that transaction began (required when more than one join property opens a transaction scope), the ownership of the Spring connection holder bound to the data source cannot be determined, or that transaction exposes its connection through a handle of its own while no JPA transaction owning it can be identified (see {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.JdbcUtil#beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} )
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedSQLException` — if acquiring a connection fails, starting or completing an internally required transaction fails, or preparing, binding, or executing a DELETE statement fails
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the total deleted-row count overflows an {@code int}
